article.title: Why a Two-Minute Review Helps Before You Send
article.why: 練習用簡單英文建立寄出前的兩分鐘檢查習慣，降低附件、收件人與語氣錯誤。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
Before you send an email, document, or chat message, take two minutes to review it. This short pause can prevent simple mistakes that create much more work later.

Start with the basics. Check the recipient. Make sure you are sending the message to the right person or group. Then check the subject line. Does it explain what the message is about? If you mention an attachment, confirm that the file is actually attached.

Next, read the first and last sentence. The first sentence should make the purpose clear. The last sentence should explain what you need from the reader. For example, “Please review this by Thursday” is clearer than “Let me know what you think.”

A short review also helps you notice emotional tone. When you write quickly, a sentence can sound colder or stronger than you intended. You may only need to add one word, such as “please,” or replace a direct command with a polite request.

Do not try to make every message perfect. The goal is to catch mistakes that are easy to fix before they reach other people. Two minutes is usually enough for recipient, attachment, main point, deadline, and tone.

This habit is especially useful when you are busy. Speed feels important, but sending the wrong file or an unclear request can cost ten or twenty minutes later. A tiny review before sending is often faster than explaining and correcting a mistake after sending.

Try a simple checklist today: right person, right file, clear purpose, clear next action. Then press send.

If the message is important, also check names, dates, and numbers. A small typo in a meeting date or price can cause confusion even when the rest of the message is correct. Reading these details separately can help because your brain often sees what you expected to write instead of what is actually on the screen.

You can make the review easier by using the same order every time. A repeated routine becomes fast, and you are less likely to forget one check.
paragraphs.zh: 寄出郵件、文件或訊息前，用兩分鐘檢查收件人、主旨、附件、第一句與最後一句。目的不是追求完美，而是先抓出容易修正、但寄出後會造成額外溝通成本的錯誤。重要訊息再特別檢查姓名、日期與數字；固定使用同一順序，可以把 review 變成快速習慣。
paragraphs.ja: メールや資料を送る前に2分だけ見直し、宛先、件名、添付、最初と最後の一文を確認します。完璧を目指すのではなく、送信後に余計な手戻りを生む小さなミスを先に防ぐのが目的です。重要な連絡では名前・日付・数字も確認し、毎回同じ順番で見ると習慣化しやすくなります。

vocabulary.usage: Check the recipient before you send.
Confirm that the attachment is included.
A small typo can create confusion.

phrases.example: Take two minutes to review before you send.
End with a clear next action.

grammar.title: Before + clause
grammar.body: Before you send 表示「在你寄出之前」，可用來描述先後順序。

business.example: Please review this by Thursday and send me any comments.
Could you confirm the attachment before we send this externally?

quiz.question: What four things can you check quickly before sending?
quiz.answer: For example: recipient, attachment, purpose, and next action.

quiz.question: Output: Write one clear final sentence for a work email.
quiz.answer: Example: Please confirm the numbers by 3 p.m. today.
